event_description: Disaster declaration for 57 counties for storms, tornadoes and flooding
Disaster declaration for Cross, Montgomery, Poinsett, Polk, Scott and Van Buren counties for tornadoes, storms and flooding
Statewide winter weather emergency for ice, snow and freezing rain
State disaster for Faulkner, Pulaski and White counties after the Vilonia and Mayflower tornado
Statewide winter weather emergency for ice and snow (feed and poultry hauling)
Disaster for Franklin, Garland, Howard, Izard, Johnson, Montgomery, Newton, Pike, Pope and Searcy counties for storms, flooding and tornadoes
Disaster for 14 counties for storms, flooding and tornadoes
Statewide state of emergency ahead of Arkansas River flooding
Statewide severe winter weather emergency for snow, sleet and ice
Conway County disaster for severe storms and flooding
Scott County disaster for storms, tornadoes and flooding
State of emergency for weekend storms including an EF-2 tornado in Logan County
Disaster for Faulkner, Lonoke, Poinsett, Pope and Pulaski counties for storms and straight-line winds
Ashley County disaster for storms and straight-line winds
Statewide state of emergency ahead of severe winter weather
Disaster for 16 counties for storms and flooding
Disaster for Columbia, Lafayette and Union counties for storms, tornadoes and flooding
Garland County disaster for storms and tornadoes
Marion and Searcy counties disaster for storms and flooding
Statewide state of emergency ahead of a sleet and snow winter storm
Disaster for Clay, Greene, Independence, Izard, Jackson, Lawrence, Nevada, Randolph, Sharp, Stone and Woodruff counties for storms and tornadoes
Disaster for Chicot, Sebastian, St. Francis and Washington counties for severe storms
Disaster for Howard, Nevada, Ouachita, Pike and Saline counties for severe winter weather
Statewide disaster declaration for the Christmas Day winter storm (snow, ice, wind and power outages)
Emergency declaration for a winter storm (freezing rain, sleet, snow and ice) that strained propane supplies
Statewide state of emergency for the June 25 thunderstorms and high winds

Proclamation DR 06-22 authorizing Governor's Disaster Fund money for the severe storms, tornadoes and flooding that began April 2, 2006 (the state share of FEMA-1636-DR), as quoted in its December 2, 2010 amendment DR 10-44.
Proclamation DR 08-07 for the severe storms and flooding that began March 18, 2008 (FEMA-1751-DR), dated March 20, 2008 in its amendments DR 10-35 and DR 10-37 (DR 10-39 gives March 24).
Proclamation DR 08-31 for the severe storms, flooding and high winds that began September 2, 2008 (FEMA-1793-DR), as quoted in its amendment DR 10-40.
Proclamation DR 08-37 for the severe storms, flooding and high winds that began September 13, 2008 (FEMA-1804-DR), as quoted in its amendment DR 10-41.
Proclamation DR 09-03 for the severe ice storms that began January 26, 2009 (FEMA-1819-DR), as quoted in its amendment DR 10-38.
Proclamation DR 09-12 for the severe storms and violent tornadoes of April 9, 2009 (FEMA-1834-DR), as quoted in its amendment DR 10-36.
Proclamation DR 09-17 for the severe thunderstorms, tornadoes and flooding beginning April 27, 2009 (FEMA-1845-DR), as quoted in its amendment DR 10-42.
Proclamation DR 09-35 for the severe storms, tornadoes and flooding beginning October 8, 2009, as quoted in its amendment DR 10-43.
Disaster declaration for 46 counties for the October 2009 storms, tornadoes and flooding, made on Saturday, November 7 (Insurance Journal, November 9, 2009).
Disaster declaration for Washington and Benton counties after the December 31, 2010 tornado, made January 1, 2011 (Insurance Journal, January 4, 2011).
State of emergency proclamation exempting utility repair trucks from federal motor carrier rules for the severe winter storm expected to cause power outages beginning February 1, 2011.
Disaster declaration for Benton, Boone, Carroll, Madison, Marion and Newton counties for the past week's severe storms and flooding, made Friday, August 16, 2013.
Disaster declarations for nine more counties, 21 in all, for the storms, tornadoes and flooding that began before Christmas, issued Tuesday, December 29, 2015.
Disaster declaration for 17 south and east Arkansas counties for flooding from heavy rains, made Thursday, March 10, 2016.
Statewide state of emergency for the deadly thunderstorms, flash flooding and high winds, declared late Sunday afternoon, April 30, 2017.
State disaster for Jonesboro after the EF3 tornado of March 28, 2020, declared at a news conference Sunday evening, March 29.
Disaster declaration for 11 south Arkansas counties for the Easter Sunday severe storms, signed Friday, April 24, 2020.
Emergency declaration in anticipation of flooding and damage from Hurricane Laura, with $250,000 for preparation, announced Wednesday afternoon, August 26, 2020.
State of emergency for record rainfall and flooding in southeast Arkansas, declared Thursday, June 10, 2021.
State of emergency after the tornadoes of Friday night, December 10, 2021 (proclamation DR 21-17, December 11, 2021, catalogued under severe storms by the Arkansas State Library).
